chunks: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Inform me about the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) — did he inherit from all the Prophets?' He said: 'Yes.' I said, 'From Adam until it reached himself?' He said: 'God did not send a Prophet except that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was more knowledgeable than him.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, "Indeed Isa ibn Maryam used to revive the dead by the permission of God." He said: "You speak the truth. And Sulayman ibn Dawud used to understand the speech of the bird, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was able to attain these stations."'

He said, then he said: 'Indeed Sulayman ibn Dawud said to the hoopoe when he missed it and doubted its matter: [27:20] What is the matter that I do not see the hoopoe, or is it among those absent? — when he missed it, he grew angry at it and said: [27:21] I will punish it with a severe punishment, or slaughter it, or it must bring me a clear authority.'

And indeed he was angry because it used to guide him to water. So this one — being a bird — had been given what Sulayman had not been given. And indeed the wind, the ants, humans, jinn, the satans, and the rebellious ones were all obedient to him, yet he did not know the water beneath the air, while the bird knew it.

And God says in His Book [13:31]: And if there were a Quran by which mountains would be moved, or the earth would be cloven, or the dead be made to speak — and we have inherited this Quran which contains that by which mountains can be moved, cities can be traversed, and the dead can be revived, and we know the water beneath the air.

And in the Book of God there are verses by which no matter is intended except that God permits it, along with what God has permitted from what He prescribed for those before us — God has made it for us in the Mother of the Book. Indeed God says [27:75]: And there is nothing concealed in the sky and the earth but it is in a clear Book.

Then he said: [35:32] Then We gave the Book as inheritance to those We chose from among Our servants. So we are those whom God Mighty and Majestic has chosen, and made us inherit this wherein is the clarification of all things.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book — the primordial divine record from which all knowledge is derived
key_terms.الْهُدْهُدُ: The hoopoe bird — used as an example of specialized knowledge granted to a creature lesser than a Prophet
key_terms.تِبْيَانُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ: The clarification/explanation of all things — referring to the Quran's comprehensive nature
key_terms.مَنْطِقُ الطَّيْرِ: The speech/language of birds — a reference to the gift granted to Sulayman (Quran 27:16)
key_terms.وَرِثَ النَّبِيِّينَ: Inherited from the Prophets — the Imam confirms the Prophet's comprehensive inheritance of all prophetic knowledge

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Kazim confirm that the Prophet Muhammad inherited knowledge from all prophets?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) confirms to a questioner that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) inherited the knowledge of all prophets before him and surpassed each of them in knowledge. The Imam then elaborates by using the Quranic story of Sulayman and the hoopoe to illustrate a profound point: even the hoopoe bird was granted a knowledge that the mighty Prophet Sulayman did not possess — knowledge of underground water — while the wind, ants, humans, jinn, and satans all obeyed Sulayman. The Imam then asserts that the Ahlulbayt have inherited the Quran in its fullness, including its miraculous capacities to move mountains, traverse lands, and revive the dead, and that they possess knowledge of the unseen (including water beneath the earth), all by God's permission through the Mother of the Book — citing Quran 13:31, 27:75, and 35:32 to establish the Imams as the 'chosen servants' who received the Book.
